items.title: 68239_Ram Ramirez oral history interview
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Even in later years I always noticed with Duke's band when Sam Woodyard would start to play a shuffle rhythm... It really used to work with that band. [INTERVIEWEE] Oh yeah.

ctx.x: I remember Charlie Parker and Dizzy Gillespie auditioned for John Kirby's orchestra, but it wasn't their style. Kirby's was mostly a shuffle rhythm type of thing, while Charlie Parker and Dizzy were playing something else. Now, the shuffle is very important. It has a backbeat to it, it's a variation, and for the Blues it's effective.
Even in later years I always noticed with Duke's band when Sam Woodyard would start to play a shuffle rhythm... It really used to work with that band.
Oh yeah. And Louis Jordan was the first so-called Rock group, to me, that ever existed. It was very popular. Louis Jordan was ahead of his time.
